_comment: DBE Grade 12 Accounting P2, November 2024. Questions + marking-guideline
answers extracted from the text layer of the PDFs in this directory
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and cross-checked by recomputing figures.
Schema follows past_papers/maths/grade11/2018/paper.json. One addition:
an optional 'information' field (array of verbatim lines) carries the
INFORMATION / pre-adjustment data block of each question section; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that section and applies to all
sub-questions of the same section.
Sub-parts that the paper prints as unnumbered bullets are given suffixed
refs (e.g. Q2.1.2a, Q3.2.3b) in printed order; Q3.2.2's printed roman
numerals are kept as Q3.2.2i .. Q3.2.2v.
memo_working reproduces the marking guideline's figures and allocation
notation (one mark / two marks / one part correct / operation / method
mark). Tick glyphs in the memo are partly image-based; per-figure tick
placement is described in words where it did not survive extraction.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Debtors' Reconciliation, Age Analysis
and VAT 40 marks 35 min; Q2 Stock Valuation 35 marks 25 min; Q3 Budgeting
40 marks 35 min; Q4 Cost Accounting 35 marks 25 min. A Financial
Indicator Formula Sheet is attached to the paper (standard NSC sheet,
not transcribed here).
Anomaly: the paper's Cash Budget extract (Q3.2, Information H) shows
Payment to creditors for Nov. 2024 as R207 012, but the memo's Creditors'
Payment Schedule November column totals R133 412 (36 800 + 96 612). Both
figures are transcribed verbatim from their sources.

questions.text: Explain TWO points of advice that you will offer to the owner. NOTE: Maximum discount is granted to debtors who settle their accounts timeously. Interest at the accepted rate is being charged.
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO valid points (part marks for partial or unclear responses): Encourage customers to pay using debit order to avoid delayed payments; Implement automated reminder system (SMS, email and phone calls) to notify customers of upcoming due dates, overdue accounts and payment confirmation; Proper screening of debtors or background check to assess debtors' financial status before credit is offered; Decrease credit limit of customers who are not adhering to credit terms / assess creditworthiness (credit score / credit history) regularly and adjust credit limits accordingly; Offer various payment options / payment plans to debtors not adhering to credit terms; Suspend / block / freeze the accounts of debtors who fail to pay on time; Utilise debt collection service / hand over debtors to debt collectors / legal action. Do not accept: offer discounts / charge interest.

questions.text: A whistle-blower has informed Nosisa that Micha (sales person) and Jack (supplier's delivery driver) have conspired to sell sunglasses at a reduced price. During an investigation it was discovered that the sunglasses sold were invoiced to the business. Nosisa has confirmed that the sunglasses were missing. Explain how Nosisa could have proven Jack and Micha guilty of the theft of the stock. Provide ONE point.
questions.topic: Stock Valuation - Internal Control and Ethics
questions.memo_answer: Any valid comment (part marks for partial or unclear responses): Use whistle-blower's statement as evidence and confirm the findings; Compare the supplier's invoice with order forms / delivery notes to check for discrepancies; Verify stock records through physical stock count upon delivery; Request tracking evidence of route and compare with delivery dates; Check CCTV footage for unusual activities when stock is delivered.

questions.text: What action should have been taken against Micha and Jack? Provide ONE point for each person.
questions.topic: Stock Valuation - Internal Control and Ethics
questions.memo_answer: Micha (salesperson), any ONE (2 marks): Conduct a fair disciplinary hearing / suspend Micha pending the outcome of hearing; Audit / investigate supplier's past transactions for other possible misconduct / fraud; File criminal complaint against him; Deduct the money from his salary / demand repayments from Micha to recover losses; Demote the salesperson / restrict him from working in similar roles within the business. Jack (supplier's driver), any ONE (2 marks): Inform the owner of his involvement and request action be taken against him; Jack should not be assigned to deal with the business anymore / prohibit Jack from entering the business property; File criminal charges against him; Pursue compensation from him if evidence confirms his involvement; Update contracts with the supplier to include penalties for future unethical behaviour.

questions.text: Comment on whether the mark-up percentage would benefit the business or not.
questions.memo_answer: Any valid explanation (part marks for partial or unclear responses): Customers will not buy / pay higher price for the product; Price-sensitive customers may choose competitors offering similar trousers for less, leading to lower sales; Regular customers may be discouraged from making repeated purchases; A decrease in sales volume could negatively affect cash flow; Stock holding period of 186 days / 6,2 months indicates lower demand which resulted in high stock levels / slow sales can lead to stock being out of fashion.

questions.text: Casual shirts: Comment on how the return of 120 casual shirts would affect the business negatively. Provide ONE point.
questions.memo_answer: Any valid explanation: High returns will make the business lose revenue / high return rate may lead to decreased future sales (customers); Lead to lower sales revenue / decrease in demand / lower gross profit; This can negatively affect the business reputation (image); Preparing returned shirts for reselling at original selling price can lead to additional cost.

questions.text: Comment on the gross profit earned by the business and the price charged for the watches. In your opinion, explain if Jabu's customers found the 2024 price reasonable. Provide figures.

questions.memo_answer: Gross profit has increased (from R960 300) to R1 237 600 / by R277 300 / by 28,9%; Number of units sold increased (from 2 910) to 3 640 / by 730 units / by 25% / total sales increased (from R2 880 900) to R3 712 800 / by R831 900 / by 28,9%; Selling price increased (from R990) to R1 020 / by R30 / by 3%, which is reasonable for the customers and is within the inflation rate. questions.text: Identify the TWO main costs that would have a positive effect on the selling price. In each case, provide a strategy that Jabu would have implemented.

questions.text: Jabu wishes to increase his profit by R300 000 during the next financial year, while maintaining the costs. Calculate the price that he would have to charge his customers in order to produce 400 extra units.
